6. Tests: which test files cover setup, provider factory, codecs (tests/agent/*), and any live tests gated by env vars.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. **Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. **Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. Finder is an application like any other: clicking the desktop, the Dock, or a Finder window (including Go to Folder) requires a Finder grant. - **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. ---

## 1. Credentials and setup

**Storage**
- Everything lives in AppConfig section `jusprin_agent` (`AgentConfiguration.cpp:13`). Keys:
  - `provider`, `model`, `enabled`, `cloud_consent`
  - one key per provider named `<provider>_api_key` (`AgentConfiguration.cpp:15`)
- Load: `load_agent_runtime` reads `enabled`, `cloud_consent`, `provider` and `model` (`AgentConfiguration.cpp:35-39`). It then loads only the active provider's key, defaulting to `openai` (`:41`).
  - Keys for other providers stay in AppConfig because commit never deletes them. That already supports holding several keys **(inferred)**.
- Commit (`make_agent_setup`, `AgentConfiguration.cpp:60-73`) writes the key, `provider`, `enabled=true` and `cloud_consent=true`, then calls `config->save()` immediately.
  - `model` is written only when it is non-empty (`:67-68`). A stale `model` saved under one provider therefore survives a switch to another provider and would be applied to it **(inferred risk)**.
- No keychain is used, on purpose (`AgentConfiguration.hpp:27-31`). The only `wxSecretStore` use is in Orca's own `src/slic3r/Utils/OrcaCloudServiceAgent.cpp:1565`, which is unrelated.
- `load_provider_api_key` (`AgentConfiguration.hpp:32`) is documented as being for printer recognition. Its only caller is `AgentConfiguration.cpp:41`.
- Provider table: `provider_profiles()` (`ProviderProfile.hpp:41-60`). Each row has id, family, endpoint, auth, default model, display name, headers and max_tokens:
  - `openai`: `gpt-5.4-mini`
  - `openrouter`: `openai/gpt-5.4-mini`, plus header `X-Title`
  - `anthropic`: `claude-opus-5-5`, plus `anthropic-version`, `max_tokens` 64000
  - `profile_for(id)` is at `:63-69`.
- `resolve_agent_runtime` (`ProviderFactory.cpp:55-85`) returns an `AgentRuntime` with `{service, availability, provider, unavailable_reason, setup}` (`AgentConfiguration.hpp:12-21`).

**Verification**
- `ProviderKeySetup::start_check` (`AgentSetup.cpp:38-54`) builds a real `ProviderAgent` through `make_provider_agent`. It sends a fixed probe turn ("Reply with the single word: ready.") with no project data (`:13-19`).
  - This is a full streaming POST through the normal turn loop, not a GET.
  - `poll()` succeeds on a ToolCall or Completed event and fails on Failed (`:63-87`).
  - `finish_ok` hands the verified, idle service back to the caller (`:99-110`).
- Supported providers: `setup_provider_supported` returns `profile_for(p) != nullptr` (`AgentSetup.cpp:23`).
- `AgentHost::handle_setup_check_key` (`AgentHost.cpp:2206-2245`):
  - parses `provider`, `apiKey`, `model` and `endpoint` from the page payload (`:2219-2223`)
  - stores them in `m_setup_pending` (`:2236`)
  - replies with `setup_status`: `checking` or `error` (`unsupported_provider`)
  - Note: the host accepts a page-supplied `endpoint` to which the key is sent (`AgentSetup.cpp:43`) **(observation)**.
- `pump_setup` (`AgentHost.cpp:2256-2284`) commits the credentials, sends `verified` (with a warning if the save failed), then calls `set_agent(service, Ready)` and the setup-completed listener.
- `handle_setup_cancel` is at `:2247-2254`. `send_setup_status` sends `{phase, provider?, elapsedMs?, error?, warning?}` (`:2188-2204`).
- `m_setup_pending` blocks user messages (`:1301-1302`) and makes `transition_busy()` true (`:3048`).
- Protocol names: `setup_check_key`/`setup_cancel` (`AgentProtocol.hpp:54-55`), `agent_status` (`:76`), `setup_status` (`:86`), `open_setup` (`:94`). The `agent_setup` capability is at `:30`.

**Page**
- `Setup.tsx`:
  - `PROVIDERS` list: anthropic / openai / openrouter, plus a disabled "other" (`:20-25`). `DEFAULT_PROVIDER='openai'` (`:28`).
  - `SetupApiKey` holds local `provider`/`key` state and calls `onCheck(provider, key)` (`:98-133`). It shows provider tabs (`:141-155`) and the footnote "Which model to use is decided for you." (`:190-192`).
  - `SetupResult` covers checking / verified (round-trip time) / error (`:198-213`). `ConnectedBanner` is at `:224-236`.
- `App.tsx:285-287` sends `setup_check_key` with only `{provider, apiKey}`; no model or endpoint. `setup_cancel` is at `:289-291`. The verified/ready handling is at `:301-315`, and `SetupApiKey` is rendered at `:553-563`.
- `protocol.ts:224-232` defines `SetupStatusPayload`. `AgentStatus = 'ready' | 'unavailable'` (`:86`). `StatePayload.agent: { status }` (`:680`).
- `store.ts:156-172` reads `agent.status` from `hello_ack`/`state`, and `:211-215` handles `agent_status` / `setup_status` / `open_setup`.
- `SetupCard.tsx` and `SetupPage.tsx` are the **print-setup** card and page, not Agent setup (`SetupCard.tsx:1-3`).

**What the host reports**
- Only `agent.status` (`ready`/`unavailable`):
  - in `hello_ack` (`AgentHost.cpp:1282`)
  - in `state` (`:928`)
  - in `agent_status` (`:3070`)
- The provider appears only transiently, in `setup_status` (`:2195-2196`).
- `AgentRuntime.provider` and `unavailable_reason` are never passed to `AgentHost`, so the page never sees them. `ShellController.cpp:268-269` passes only availability, service and setup.

## 2. Agent construction

**Factory**
- `make_provider_agent(profile, api_key, model, endpoint, transport, listeners)` (`ProviderFactory.cpp:29-46`):
  - copies the profile and overrides `model`/`endpoint` when they are non-empty
  - picks the codec once, by family (`codec_for`, `:12-19`)
- `ProviderAgentConfig` = `{profile, api_key, usage_listener, refusal_listener}` (`ProviderAgent.hpp:27-37`). It is held as `m_config` (`:71`) and fixed for the agent's lifetime.
- `max_tokens` exists only as `profile.max_tokens`.
- `OpenAIResponsesAgent` (`OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp:10-26`) is a legacy wrapper used only by tests and `shell_harness`.

**Who builds it, and when**
- Docked pane, once at shell install: `ShellController.cpp:265` calls `load_agent_runtime`, then constructs `AgentPane(... service, setup ...)` (`:268-270`).
  - `AgentWebView.cpp:69-70` constructs the `AgentHost` with that service.
  - The host holds one agent: `AgentHost.hpp:489` (`m_agent`), set in the constructor (`AgentHost.cpp:673`).
- PrinterPanel builds its own runtime on every open (`PrinterPanel.cpp:79-82`). It uses in-memory persistence (`:74`).

**Rebuilds**
- `AgentHost::set_agent` (`AgentHost.cpp:3082-3091`) replaces the agent. It is a silent no-op while `agent_busy()`.
- After setup in the dock: `pump_setup` installs the verified service (`:2281`).
- After setup in PrinterPanel:
  1. its listener calls `agent_configured` (`PrinterPanel.cpp:156-158`)
  2. that becomes `mark_agent_config_possibly_changed` (`ShellController.cpp:533`)
  3. on the next tab change, `load_agent_runtime` runs again and its result goes to `set_agent` (`:1189-1193`).
  - The flag is cleared before `set_agent`, so a busy host drops the update **(inferred)**.
- Nothing else rebuilds the agent when settings change.

**Turn flow and where model/profile are read**
1. `begin_reply` (`AgentHost.cpp:2370`) leads to `begin_stream` (`:2417-2438`). That calls `make_agent_request` (`:2440-2650`, with no provider/model fields) and then `m_agent->start(request)` (`:2436`).
2. `ProviderAgent::start` (`ProviderAgent.cpp:233-248`) calls `begin_transcript` (`:173-231`), then `post()`.
3. `post()` (`ProviderAgent.cpp:277-299`) is where the profile is read on every request:
   - `m_codec->build(m_transcript, m_config.profile, m_kind)` (`:284`)
   - URL = `m_config.profile.endpoint` (`:286`)
   - auth from `m_config.api_key` (`:287`)
   - profile headers (`:288`)
4. Error text uses `profile.display_name` (`:490-506`). `ready()` requires key, model and endpoint (`:165-169`).
5. Tool continuations call `post()` again (`:436`), and pause_turn resends (`:360`). Every request in a turn therefore uses the same `m_config`.

Title generation shares the same `m_agent`, and therefore the same provider and model (`AgentHost.cpp:2968-3030`, start at `:2998`).

**What must change for per-turn choice (inferred):** today provider, model and key are all fixed in `m_config`, and the codec is fixed per family. Two options:
- Option 1: carry a choice on `AgentRequest` (`AgentService.hpp:96-121`) and have `ProviderAgent` use a per-turn profile copy and codec.
- Option 2: have `AgentHost` build or select a `ProviderAgent` per turn with `make_provider_agent`, re-reading that provider's key from AppConfig.

## 3. Request building

**Responses** (`ResponsesCodec.cpp:113-134`)
- Every request sends header `Idempotency-Key = <request_id>-request-<seq>` (`:116`).
- Reply body: `model`, `store:false`, `stream:true`, `parallel_tool_calls:true`, `instructions`, `tools`, `input` (`:131-132`).
- Title body: `model`, `store:false`, `stream:true`, `instructions` (title text), `input`. No tools (`:119-120`).
- Tools: `{type:function, name, description, strict, parameters}` (`:31-44`).
- Not sent: `max_output_tokens`, `reasoning`, `include`, and any cache fields.
- `store:false` without `include:["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` means the reasoning items it replays may not carry their content **(inferred)**.

**Anthropic** (`AnthropicCodec.cpp:251-281`)
- Body: `model`, `max_tokens` (`profile.max_tokens`), `stream:true`, and `system` as a single text block with `cache_control: ephemeral`. `system` is omitted if empty (`:278-279`).
- `messages`; `tools` only when it is not a title request and tools exist (`:274-275`).
- Tools: `{name, description, input_schema (strict-projected), strict}`, with `cache_control` on the last tool (`:74-89`).
- A `cache_control` breakpoint goes on the last block of the newest user message (`:260-264`).
- No `thinking` and no `tool_choice` are sent; a test asserts this (`test_anthropic_codec.cpp:195-215`). `ProviderProfile.hpp:53-55` notes that `max_tokens` bounds thinking that this model cannot turn off.
- The parser accumulates `thinking_delta` and `signature_delta` into blocks (`:334-338`).

**Replay of earlier turns versus within-turn steps**
- `TurnTranscript.opening` = `request.conversation` (`ProviderAgent.cpp:178`). It is a list of `AgentConversationContext` = `{role, text, issue_context, call_id, tool, arguments_json, output_json}` (`AgentService.hpp:35-49`).
  - Built in `AgentHost.cpp:2554-2605` from stored message text and stored tool activities.
  - Results over 16 KiB are replaced by an omission note (`:2596-2599`). History is trimmed to 64 KiB (`:2616-2640+`).
- Responses replays opening entries as role/content messages, or as `function_call` + `function_call_output` without item ids (`ResponsesCodec.cpp:66-82`).
- Anthropic replays them as `tool_use` + `tool_result`, with `developer` mapped to system (`AnthropicCodec.cpp:174-194`).
- Within a turn, `steps[].assistant_turn` is replayed verbatim:
  - Responses: output items, "reasoning included" (`ResponsesCodec.cpp:85-87`)
  - Anthropic: content blocks, "thinking included" (`AnthropicCodec.cpp:215-217`)
- **Confirmed: no provider-specific reasoning or thinking crosses turns.** `assistant_turn` lives only in the per-turn `m_transcript`, which is reset in `begin_transcript` (`ProviderAgent.cpp:175`). `ConversationMessage` stores only text and metadata (`AgentProtocol.hpp:161-181`).
  - Cross-provider history is therefore already neutral. A live test covers an OpenAI call id in Anthropic history (`test_provider_live.cpp:511`).

## 4. Conversation storage

**Per-chat metadata**
- Each chat is an object in `m_doc["conversations"]`, created by `create_conversation` (`ProjectStateDocument.cpp:549-566`). Fields: `id` (`c-N`), `seq`, `title`, `titleSource` (`default|manual|generated`), `createdAt`, `setupIntent`, `messages`.
- `resumeCheckpoint` is added later (`:625-629`).
- Accessed through the private `conversation_json(id)` (`:744-758`). This is a natural home for `{provider, model, thinking}` **(inferred)**.
- `ConversationInfo` struct (`ProjectStateDocument.hpp:29-37`) is read in `conversations()` (`.cpp:515-543`). It goes to the page via `conversation_list_json` (`AgentHost.cpp:26-33`) as `{id, title, createdAt, updatedAt, preview}`.
- Title logic: `needs_conversation_title` / `rename_conversation` (`.cpp:647-673`).

**Compatibility**
- `kSchemaVersion = 3` (`.hpp:178`).
- `load()` (`.cpp:440-466`):
  - a missing or non-integer `schemaVersion` is treated as Corrupt
  - a version newer than the build is treated as Corrupt, so it is never edited (`:449-453`)
  - otherwise the parsed document is merged onto `fresh_document()` (`:376-399`), keeping unknown keys, and a lower version returns `Migrated`
- Readers use `value(key, default)` throughout, so a missing key is harmless (for example `:519`, `:678`). Legacy fallbacks: `titleSource` (`:651-655`), activity `source` (`:349`).
- A new optional per-chat key needs no schema bump, and older builds preserve it **(inferred from merge and the test below)**.
- Tests: "unknown fields survive a load-edit-save cycle" (`test_project_state.cpp:332`).
- The PrinterPanel chat is in-memory only (`PrinterPanel.cpp:74`).

## 5. Network calls

- No HTTP GET exists in the Agent code, and nothing fetches a model list. The setup check is a streaming POST through `ProviderAgent`.
- `IAgentHttpTransport` has only `post()` and `cancel()` (`AgentTransport.hpp:48-55`).
- The underlying client is `Slic3r::Http` (`Utils/Http.hpp`): `Http::get` (`:82`), `perform()` (`:186`) runs on a background thread, `perform_sync()` (`:188`). It offers `on_complete` / `on_error` / `on_progress` and `timeout_*` / `size_limit`.
- **Async pattern A (the Agent's):** `OpenAIHttpTransport` (`OpenAIHttpTransport.cpp:17-69`) uses `Http::post(...).perform()` with callbacks that hold a `weak_ptr` to state behind a mutex.
  1. `ProviderAgent::accept_http` queues the events under `m_mutex` (`ProviderAgent.cpp:301-305`).
  2. `poll()` / `parse_available()` drains them on the GUI thread (`:439-488`).
  3. The driver is the shell's 33 ms runtime timer (`ShellController.cpp:514`), which calls `pump_stream` / `pump_tools` / `pump_setup` (`:207-211`). PrinterPanel has its own pump (`PrinterPanel.cpp:389`).
- **Async pattern B (the GET example):** `HostLaneReader.cpp:84-106` runs `Http::get(...).perform_sync()` on a detached `std::thread` (`:155-161`). Results go into a shared `HostReadings` that the GUI polls (`host_status`, `:146-164`). Exit safety comes from `StopReadsAtExit` (`:20-49`).
